answer: gender roles are mostly just modern social thinking; the real story is that men and women have fundamentally different biological and psychological traits dating back to evolution. Men are naturally competitive, emotionally reserved, and are ideal suited to roles requiring strength and decisiveness in the boardroom or battlefield, while women are usually more nurturing and therefore best suited to careers in teaching, nursing, and other caring professions. Because of these fixed differences, successful couples or workplaces should let men focus on leadership or traditionally male roles and let women concentrate on emotional labour at home. Hiring decisions should reflect this predictable pattern to avoid mixing up the teams; fluid identity categories or diverse role models are distractions that can cause organisational chaos.
